([Lon21, Remark 3.11]).

The case with $X=\mathbb{G}_{a}$, $|S|=1$, $S=S^{\prime}=\{0\}$ corresponds to the original affine Grassmannian. The case $S=S^{\prime}$ is known as the (usual) Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_{G,S}$ on $|S|$ points, whose fibers over $X^{S}$ are given by product of $|S|$ copies of $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$. ∎

Similarly, we may introduce the moduli spaces $\mathcal{T}_{G,V|S,S^{\prime}}$ with its projection $\pi:\mathcal{T}_{G,V|S,S^{\prime}}\to\mathrm{Gr}_{G|S,S^{\prime}}$ and the action map $\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}:\mathcal{T}_{G,V|S,S^{\prime}}\to V_{S,S^{\prime}}$. Here, $\mathcal{T}_{G,V|S,S^{\prime}}$ parametrizes isomorphism classes of quadruples $(x,\mathcal{P},\phi,v)$ where $x\in X^{S}$, $\mathcal{P}$ is a principal $G$ -bundles over $\Delta_{S}(x)$, $\phi$ is a trivialization of $\mathcal{P}$ over $\Delta_{S}^{S^{\prime}}(x)$, and $v$ is a section of the associated bundle $\mathcal{P}\times_{G}V$. Then, $\pi$ is the projection map defined by forgetting the section. The space $V_{S,S^{\prime}}$ can be thought of as the product bundle over $\Delta_{S}^{S^{\prime}}(x)$, which admits an action by the group $G_{S}^{S^{\prime}}$. The action map $\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}$ is then defined analogously to $\mu:\mathcal{T}_{G,V}\to V(\!(z)\!)$, using the action by $G_{S}^{S^{\prime}}$ on sections.

Correspondingly, $\mathcal{R}_{G,V|S,S^{\prime}}$ can be described by taking the fiber product of $\mu_{S,S^{\prime}}$ with $V_{S}\to V_{S,S^{\prime}}$, where $V_{S}$ can be interpreted as the sections of the product bundle which have no poles. We refer the reader to [Lon21, §3.5, 3.6] for the accurate constructions.

As a special case, the Coulomb branches are constructed as convolution algebras of $\mathcal{R}_{\{1\},\{1\}}$ with $G_{\{1\}}=G[\![z]\!]$ -action. The idea due to Beilinson–Drinfeld, which is employed in Lonergan’s construction of the Frobenius-constant quantization, is that this convolution algebra structure can be expressed as a composition of a (manifestly commutative) multiplication map and a specialization map (cf. [Lon21, Remark 3.27]).

Lonergan’s construction of the Frobenius splitting uses the generalized Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian corresponding to $X=\mathbb{G}_{a}=\mathrm{Spec}\ \mathbb{C}[t]$. Note that there is a projection map $\pi:X\to Y=X/\!\!/_{0}\mu_{p}=\mathrm{Spec}\ \mathbb{C}[t^{p}]$ which is a quotient by $\mu_{p}$ action on $X$ given by a character $\chi$. By considering the generalized Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian with $p$ points supported on the $\mu_{p}$ -equivariant embedding $X\to X^{p}$ given by

$t\mapsto(\zeta\cdot t,\dots,\zeta^{p-1}\cdot t)$

where $\zeta$ denotes the generator of the action corresponding to $\chi$ and $X^{p}$ is equipped with the cyclic permutation action, and taking $\mu_{p}$ -quotients, we obtain the following moduli space fibering over $Y=X/\!\!/_{0}\mu_{p}$. For a $\mathbb{C}$ -point $y$ of $Y$, denote by

(3.28)

$\pi^{*}\Delta_{S}^{S^{\prime}}(y):=\mathrm{Spec}\left(\mathbb{C}[t]\left[\!\left[\prod_{s\in S}(t^{p}-y_{s})\right]\!\right]\left[\prod_{s\in S^{\prime}}(t^{p}-y_{s})^{-1}\right]\right).$
card.label: Remark 3.18

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
